title: Cachitos de jamón (Venezuelan ham-filled bread rolls)

ingredients.name: eggs, one for the dough and one for glazing
white cheese or mild cheddar, cubed (optional)

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then add the warm milk, 1 egg and butter and knead for 10 minutes into a soft, smooth dough.
Cover and let it rise for about 1 hour until doubled in size.
Divide the dough into 8 pieces and roll each into a long oval or triangle about 3 mm thick.
Scatter chopped ham, and cheese if using, along the wide end of each piece and roll up towards the point, as for a croissant. Curve slightly into a crescent.
Place on a lined baking tray with the tips tucked underneath, cover and rise for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 190 C.
Brush with the remaining beaten egg and bake for 18 to 22 minutes until deep golden. Cool slightly and serve warm.

title: Chupe andino (Venezuelan Andes chicken, potato and cheese soup)

ingredients.name: ears of corn, each cut into 3 pieces
white cheese (queso fresco or mild feta), cubed

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and gently cook the onion and garlic for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the chicken, stock, corn and carrot with 1 teaspoon of salt. Bring to a boil and simmer covered for 25 minutes.
Add the potatoes and simmer for another 15 to 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the potatoes are tender.
Remove the chicken, shred the meat off the bones and return it to the pot.
Pour in the milk, warm gently without letting it boil and check the seasoning.
Stir in the cheese and cilantro, ladle into bowls and serve immediately.

title: Guasacaca (Venezuelan avocado and herb sauce)
steps: Put the bell pepper, onion, garlic, cilantro, parsley, chili and vinegar in a blender and pulse until finely chopped.
Add the avocado flesh and blend until smooth but still a little textured.
With the blender running at low speed, drizzle in the oil until the sauce looks glossy.
Season with salt and, if needed, a splash more vinegar.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes so the flavors blend.
Serve with grilled meat, chicken, empanadas, arepas or tequeños.

title: Mandocas (Venezuelan plantain and cornmeal rings)

ingredients.name: grated white cheese (queso fresco or mild feta)
papelón or brown sugar, dissolved in 150 ml warm water

steps: Boil the plantain in water for 15 to 20 minutes until very soft, then drain and mash it smooth.
Stir the papelón water and salt into the plantain.
Add the cornmeal and cheese and knead until you get a soft, smooth dough that does not stick to your hands. Add a little more water if it is crumbly or a little more cornmeal if sticky.
Take golf-ball-sized pieces of dough, roll into ropes and join the ends to make a ring about 7 cm across, or flatten into discs with a hole in the middle.
Heat about 5 cm of oil to 170 C and fry the rings in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with butter and extra cheese, and a cup of coffee.

title: Papelon con limon (Venezuelan unrefined cane sugar and lime drink)

ingredients.name: papelón or panela (unrefined cane sugar), or dark muscovado sugar

steps: Break the papelón into pieces and put them in a pan with 400 ml of the water.
Heat gently, stirring, until fully dissolved, about 5 minutes. Strain to remove any bits.
Pour the syrup into a large jug and add the remaining cold water.
Stir in the lime juice, starting with the juice of 3 limes, and taste, adding more lime or a little water to balance.
Chill for 1 hour.
Serve over plenty of ice.

title: Perico (Venezuelan scrambled eggs with tomato and onion)
steps: Melt the butter in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Cook the onion, bell pepper and scallions for about 4 minutes, until soft.
Add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until they release their juice and thicken a little.
Beat the eggs lightly with a pinch of salt and pepper and pour them over the vegetables.
Stir gently and slowly with a spatula for 2 to 3 minutes, just until the eggs are softly set; do not let them dry out.
Serve immediately, traditionally with warm arepas.

title: Polvorosas (Venezuelan crumbly butter cookies)
steps: Heat the oven to 170 C and line a baking tray with parchment.
Cream the butter and sugar until pale and fluffy, then beat in the vanilla and milk.
Sift together the flour, cornstarch and salt and fold into the butter mixture to make a soft dough.
Roll the dough into balls about 3 cm across, or roll out 1 cm thick and cut into rounds, and place on the tray 3 cm apart.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until set and barely golden at the edges.
Cool on the tray for 10 minutes, then dust generously with powdered sugar once cold.

title: Quesillo (Venezuelan caramel milk custard)
steps: Heat the oven to 170 C and bring a kettle of water to a boil.
Melt the sugar in a small pan over medium heat, without stirring, until it becomes a deep amber caramel. Pour immediately into a 20 cm cake or flan tin and tilt to coat the base and sides.
Blend or whisk the condensed milk, milk, eggs and vanilla until smooth, then strain through a sieve.
Pour the custard into the caramelised tin and cover tightly with foil.
Set the tin in a larger roasting pan and pour hot water around it to come halfway up the sides. Bake for 50 to 60 minutes until set with a slight wobble in the center.
Cool, then chill for at least 4 hours or overnight before running a knife around the edge and turning out onto a plate.
